turns.question: Explain Infosys's latest results in simple words
turns.answer:
**What happened:** Infosys’s latest reported quarter in the data is the quarter ended **June 30, 2026**. Revenue was **₹48,211 crore**, up from ₹46,402 crore in the previous quarter. Earnings were **₹7,769 crore**, down from ₹8,501 crore.

**Why:** Earnings per share (EPS)—the profit allocated to each share—was **₹19.17**, just above the estimate of ₹19.12. The previous quarter’s EPS was higher at ₹20.98, so the latest quarter was a step down from that strong result. The data available here doesn’t explain what caused earnings to fall quarter-on-quarter.

**In context:** Revenue has risen in each of the last four quarters shown, from **₹44,490 crore** to ₹48,211 crore. Profit has moved less steadily: it fell in one quarter, rose sharply in the next, and then declined. That means the recent revenue growth has not translated into steadily rising quarterly earnings. The company’s reported operating margin—the share of revenue left after operating costs—was **21.2%** on the available metrics, but those figures are not identified as specific to this latest quarter.

**What to watch:** The next results are listed for **October 23, 2026**. They can help show whether revenue keeps growing and whether profit and margins strengthen or weaken. There are no news headlines available here to explain the latest quarter’s profit decline.

**What this means for you:** Infosys has shown steadily rising revenue in the recent quarters, but earnings have fluctuated; the next report will give a clearer view of whether that pattern continues.
